\documentclass[11pt]{article}\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,amsthm}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}\newtheorem{remark}{Remark}
\title{Fr\'echet Dispersion and the Exact Collar-Failure Charge}\author{}\date{21 July 2026}
\begin{document}\maketitle
\begin{abstract}We identify the incident link energy with the Fr\'echet energy of its staple family.  This corrects the deterministic collar-failure charge from $\eta^2/2$ to $\eta^2$ and introduces dispersion as the natural retained variable.\end{abstract}
Let $G=SU(2)$ carry its bi-invariant distance and let $S_1,\dots,S_m$ be the staples incident on a link $U$. Define
\[\Phi(C)=\sum_i d(C,S_i)^2,\quad \mathcal D=\inf_C\Phi(C),\quad R=\inf_C\max_i d(C,S_i).\]
\begin{theorem}[Exact identity and charges]For every $U$,
\[E(U):=\sum_i d(I,US_i)^2=\Phi(U^{-1})\ge\mathcal D.\]
If $R>\eta$, then $E(U)>\eta^2$ for every $U$.\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}Bi-invariance gives $d(I,US_i)=d(U^{-1},S_i)$.  The first assertion follows by summation and minimization. If $R>\eta$, no center contains all staples in an $\eta$-ball. Taking the particular center $U^{-1}$ gives an index with $d(U^{-1},S_i)>\eta$; its squared contribution already exceeds $\eta^2$.\end{proof}
With heat-kernel weight $\exp[-E/(2t)]$, the corrected local exponent is $\eta^2/(2t)$, twice the earlier diameter-only value $\eta^2/(4t)$.  The result is gauge invariant because a common endpoint gauge action transports centers and preserves all distances.
\begin{remark}This is a deterministic action statement. Radial Haar entropy, witness multiplicity, conditional normalization, retained states, and volume uniformity remain separate. No physical basin entry follows.\end{remark}
